english_fig_002.original_caption: Distribution of Quantifiers and Operations in Categorical, Approximate Number Generation, Disjunctive Reasoning, and Conjunctive Reasoning.
english_fig_002.modified_caption: Distribution of Quantifiers and Operations in Categorical, Approximate Number Generation, and Disjunctive & Conjunctive Reasoning. The Categorical pie chart comprises four segments: Universal Quantifiers (29.07%), Negation (27.91%), Limiter (27.91%), and Existential Quantifiers (15.12%). In the Approximate Number Generation chart, Comparative Relationships constitute the largest share at approximately 48%, followed by Approximate Quantities at 33.26% and Absolute Absence at 18.71%. The Disjunctive & Conjunctive chart shows a near-even split, with Conjunctive slightly dominating at 54.51% over Disjunctive at 45.49%.

modifications.claim: Comparative Relationships constitute the largest share at approximately 48%
modifications.reality: Comparative Relationships is 36.26%, not 48% — Approximate Quantities (45.03%) is actually the largest share

modifications.claim: Approximate Quantities at 33.26%
modifications.reality: Approximate Quantities is actually 45.03% — a 26% understatement

modifications.claim: Conjunctive slightly dominating at 54.51% over Disjunctive at 45.49%
modifications.reality: Disjunctive is 49.51% and Conjunctive is 50.49% — the gap is swapped and exaggerated from ~1% to ~9%

correct_elements: chart titles (Categorical, Approximate Number Generation, Disjunctive & Conjunctive)
Categorical slice names and percentages (all four correct)

english_fig_005.modified_caption: Coverage as a function of the number of completions (k) for Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. All four models exhibit monotonically increasing coverage with additional completions on a logarithmic x-axis from 2^0 to 2^8. The 3B models begin at approximately 0.42 coverage and reach roughly 0.92 at k=256, while the 1B variants start near 0.22 and plateau at approximately 0.72 by k=128 with minimal further gains. Notably, fine-tuning provides a consistent advantage of approximately 5 percentage points for the 1B model throughout the scaling curve, whereas the 3B base and fine-tuned variants remain largely indistinguishable.

modifications.claim: 1B variants plateau at approximately 0.72 by k=128 with minimal further gains
modifications.reality: 1B variants reach approximately 0.85-0.88 at k=256 and do not plateau at k=128 — understated by ~18% and false plateau claim

modifications.claim: fine-tuning provides a consistent advantage of approximately 5 percentage points for the 1B model
modifications.reality: Llama-1B and Llama-1B + FT lines nearly completely overlap — fine-tuning provides no visible advantage

modifications.claim: 3B base and fine-tuned variants remain largely indistinguishable
modifications.reality: This is actually true for the 3B pair but stated to make the false 1B fine-tuning claim seem more contrastive — the misdirection is in the 1B claim, not this one

correct_elements: axis labels (Number of completions k, Coverage)
four model names (Llama-3B, Llama-3B+FT, Llama-1B, Llama-1B+FT)
all models show monotonically increasing coverage

english_fig_009.original_caption: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity.
english_fig_009.modified_caption: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring shows that nearly half of all samples (49.0%) exhibit zero ambiguity standard deviation (Std: 0.0), followed by Std: 0.47 at 38.0%, with the remaining samples distributed between Std: 0.82 at 7.0% and Std: 0.94 at 5.0%. In the inner ring, Max Ambiguity of 1 accounts for approximately 39.0% of samples, Max: 2 represents the largest inner-ring segment at 47.7%, and Max: 3 comprises 14.2%. The two rings together indicate that the majority of samples exhibit low ambiguity across both measures.

modifications.claim: Max Ambiguity of 1 accounts for approximately 39.0%
modifications.reality: Max: 1 is actually 47.7% — the values of Max: 1 and Max: 2 are swapped

modifications.claim: Max: 2 represents the largest inner-ring segment at 47.7%
modifications.reality: Max: 2 is actually 39.0% (or 38.0%) — it is not the largest inner-ring segment; Max: 1 is

modifications.claim: Std: 0.82 at 7.0% and Std: 0.94 at 5.0%
modifications.reality: Std: 0.82 is actually 5.0% and Std: 0.94 is actually 7.0% — the values are swapped in the claim

outer ring = Ambiguity Std, inner ring = Max Ambiguity
legend descriptions present for both rings
overall interpretation that most samples have low ambiguity

english_fig_033.original_caption: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where “Base” denotes LLM without editing.
english_fig_033.modified_caption: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes LLM without editing. The x-axis shows co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, while the y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %). All six methods show improving accuracy with increasing co-occurrence frequency. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. MEND and MEMIT follow as the next best performers, with MEND reaching approximately 56% and MEMIT approximately 55%. Notably, IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT, surpassing it at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The Base model exhibits the lowest performance throughout, plateauing at approximately 44%.

modifications.claim: IKE surpasses FT at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52%
modifications.reality: IKE reaches approximately 49% at highest frequency, and FT reaches approximately 47-48% — IKE is slightly above FT throughout, not just above 10^2. The 52% value is inflated by ~6%

modifications.claim: IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT
modifications.reality: Both IKE and FT show similar gradual slopes. FT actually has a comparable or slightly steeper slope from left to right

modifications.claim: Base model plateauing at approximately 44%
modifications.reality: Base model shows a slight increase from about 37-38% to about 44%, but it is not clearly plateauing — it levels off around 43-44% but calling it a 'plateau' overstates the flatness since it does increase in the middle range

correct_elements: six methods named correctly (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, ROME)
all methods show improving accuracy with co-occurrence

english_fig_057.modified_caption: Training loss curves over iterations for Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), and four SepLLM configurations. All models start with loss values exceeding 3.4 and converge as training progresses to 140,000 iterations. The Vanilla model achieves the lowest final loss at approximately 2.45, while StrmLLM (n=64) converges to roughly 2.60, showing a notable gap from the SepLLM variants. Among the SepLLM configurations, the H/T variant reaches the lowest loss at approximately 2.49, with SepLLM (n=128) settling at approximately 2.55, slightly above both the base SepLLM (n=64) and SepLLM (n=64, H) which converge near 2.51-2.52. The most rapid decrease in loss occurs within the first 20,000 iterations for all models, after which convergence slows considerably.

modifications.claim: SepLLM (n=128) settling at approximately 2.55
modifications.reality: SepLLM (n=128) converges to just above 2.50, very close to the other SepLLM variants — 2.55 overstates its final loss by ~0.05

modifications.claim: SepLLM (n=128) slightly above both base SepLLM (n=64) and SepLLM (n=64, H)
modifications.reality: SepLLM (n=128) actually converges slightly below SepLLM (n=64) and SepLLM (n=64, H), not above them — the ranking among SepLLM variants is inverted

modifications.claim: StrmLLM (n=64) converges to roughly 2.60, showing a notable gap from the SepLLM variants
modifications.reality: StrmLLM does converge higher than SepLLM variants but at approximately 2.60 vs ~2.50-2.52, characterizing this as 'notable' exaggerates a modest gap and the value is approximately right but the framing amplifies the difference

correct_elements: StrmLLM converges higher than SepLLM variants

english_fig_075.original_caption: The effect of context masking on case tasks groupby by language family. Error bars indicate the standard deviation.
english_fig_075.modified_caption: The effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family, with error bars indicating standard deviation. Six model configurations are compared across nine language families: mBERT-L2, XLM-L2, mBERT-R2, XLM-R2, mBERT-B2, and XLM-B2. The IE-Indic family shows the largest effects overall, with most configurations reaching between 17 and 25, while Uralic and Isolate families show near-zero effects across all models. Notably, IE-Germanic exhibits consistently higher effects than IE-Romance across all configurations, with XLM-B2 reaching approximately 20 in IE-Germanic. The Semitic family displays the widest error bars overall, suggesting high variability, and the mBERT-L2 bars in Semitic reach approximately 15. In IE-Slavic, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2) dominate over the L2 and R2 variants, with effects approximately twice as large.

modifications.claim: IE-Germanic exhibits consistently higher effects than IE-Romance across all configurations
modifications.reality: IE-Germanic and IE-Romance show similar magnitudes overall. IE-Romance appears comparable or even slightly higher for some configurations (e.g., XLM-B2). The claim of consistent superiority is false

modifications.claim: XLM-B2 reaching approximately 20 in IE-Germanic
modifications.reality: XLM-B2 (red bar) in IE-Germanic reaches approximately 15, not 20 — a 33% overstatement

modifications.claim: mBERT-L2 bars in Semitic reach approximately 15
modifications.reality: mBERT-L2 (light blue) in Semitic reaches approximately 11, not 15 — a 36% overstatement

correct_elements: nine language family names listed correctly
IE-Indic shows largest effects overall (17-25 range)
B2 variants tend to show larger effects

english_fig_085.original_caption: Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline Mistral-v0.2 and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data. Each group represents tokens categorized into different clinical specialties. Each color means that the same model is further fine-tuned on each specialty data.
english_fig_085.modified_caption: Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline MistralV0.2-Base and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data. The chart displays six specialty groups along the x-axis (Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, Pediatrics), with the y-axis showing negative log probability ranging from approximately -27 to -22. Within each group, the MistralV0.2-Base bar (light blue) consistently shows the highest negative log probability, indicating weaker token predictions at baseline. Among the fine-tuned models, the Gastro-tuned variant achieves the lowest negative log probability across most specialty groups, suggesting strong cross-specialty transfer. Notably, the Infect group shows the largest overall bar heights, with baseline reaching approximately -23.5, while the Cardio group exhibits the smallest spread between baseline and fine-tuned variants at roughly 1.5 units.

modifications.claim: Gastro-tuned variant achieves the lowest negative log probability across most specialty groups
modifications.reality: The fine-tuned variants show relatively similar performance within each group — there is no clear single variant that dominates. The bars within each specialty group are close in height for the fine-tuned models

modifications.claim: Infect group shows the largest overall bar heights, with baseline reaching approximately -23.5
modifications.reality: Cardio bars are overall taller (closer to -22), not Infect. Infect bars are actually shorter overall (more negative). The ranking of which group has tallest bars is inverted

modifications.claim: Cardio group exhibits the smallest spread between baseline and fine-tuned variants at roughly 1.5 units
modifications.reality: Cardio actually shows bars that are taller overall (closer to -22) and the spread claim is fabricated — the spread appears similar across groups

correct_elements: six specialty groups correctly named (Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, Pediatrics)
MistralV0.2-Base bar is consistently the tallest (highest neg log prob) in each group
multiple fine-tuned variants shown per group
axis label (Negative log probability, Per-specialty terms)

english_fig_136.original_caption: Number of participants (N=6) who highlighted each evaluation criterion as beneficial.
english_fig_136.modified_caption: Number of participants (N=6) who highlighted each evaluation criterion as beneficial. The horizontal bar chart displays seven criteria ranked by participant endorsement. Relevant FCs was unanimously selected by all 6 participants, followed by FC Summary at 5. Relevance Explanation and Clarity and Simplicity each received 3 endorsements. Overall Summary was highlighted by 2 participants, while Filters and Veracity Explanation each received 1. Notably, the top three criteria — Relevant FCs, FC Summary, and Relevance Explanation — together account for approximately 82% of all endorsements, indicating a strong consensus around content retrieval and summarization features over interface and transparency elements such as Filters and Veracity Explanation.

modifications.claim: top three criteria together account for approximately 82% of all endorsements
modifications.reality: Top three (6+5+3=14) out of total (6+5+3+3+2+1+1=21) is 66.7%, not 82% — overstated by 15 percentage points

modifications.claim: indicating a strong consensus around content retrieval and summarization features over interface and transparency elements
modifications.reality: This interpretive framing imposes a false dichotomy — Clarity and Simplicity (3 endorsements) is arguably an interface feature but is not grouped that way. The characterization nudges toward a narrative not supported by the distribution

modifications.claim: ranked by participant endorsement
modifications.reality: Relevance Explanation and Clarity and Simplicity are tied at 3 each, so the chart is not strictly ranked — this subtly implies a hierarchy between the tied items that does not exist

correct_elements: Relevant FCs is highest, Filters and Veracity Explanation are lowest

english_fig_171.original_caption: Training rewards of LLaMA-3.1 8B on the Easy and Hard training set.
english_fig_171.modified_caption: Training rewards of LLaMA-3.1 8B on the Easy and Hard training sets, displayed as two vertically stacked line plots. In the Easy Training Set (top panel), both Llama-On-Policy-Easy (teal) and Llama-LUFFY-Easy (red) start near 0.0 and increase over 500 steps, with LUFFY reaching approximately 0.4 and On-Policy reaching approximately 0.35 at step 500. In the Hard Training Set (bottom panel), Llama-LUFFY-Hard shows steady improvement from near 0.0 to approximately 0.2 by step 500, while Llama-On-Policy-Hard initially rises to approximately 0.05 before declining back toward 0.0 after step 150. Notably, the performance gap between the two methods is substantially wider on the Easy set, where LUFFY maintains a consistent lead of approximately 0.10 throughout training, compared to the Hard set where their trajectories only clearly diverge after step 200.

modifications.claim: performance gap between the two methods is substantially wider on the Easy set
modifications.reality: The gap is actually much wider on the Hard set (~0.2 vs ~0.0) than on the Easy set (~0.05 difference). This is a direct inversion of the key finding

modifications.claim: LUFFY maintains a consistent lead of approximately 0.10 throughout training on Easy set
modifications.reality: The gap on the Easy set is much smaller, approximately 0.03-0.05, not 0.10 — and the two lines are very close together for much of the training

modifications.claim: trajectories only clearly diverge after step 200 on the Hard set
modifications.reality: On the Hard set, the trajectories diverge much earlier — On-Policy drops to ~0.0 by step 100-150 while LUFFY continues climbing, so divergence is apparent by step 100

correct_elements: chart type (two vertically stacked line plots)
panel titles (Easy Training Set, Hard Training Set)
four line labels correct (Llama-On-Policy-Easy, Llama-LUFFY-Easy, Llama-On-Policy-Hard, Llama-LUFFY-Hard)
